title: Genealogy-triggered hard cooldown is a useful drift signal but not a robust safety controller; online conformal methods offer frequency calibration rather than per-run variance caps

public_sources.title: Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Distribution Shift
public_sources.result: Provides long-run coverage-frequency control under arbitrary distribution shift. This is potentially useful for calibrating a moving uncertainty set, but it is not an instantaneous per-run containment guarantee and therefore cannot by itself turn the r125 1.30 conditional variance cap into an unconditional run-level cap.

public_sources.title: Online conformal prediction with decaying step sizes
public_sources.authors: Anastasios N. Angelopoulos, Rina Foygel Barber, Stephen Bates
public_sources.result: Retains retrospective coverage guarantees for arbitrary sequences while improving stable-regime pointwise behavior; again the directly stated adversarial guarantee is sequence-level rather than a one-step coefficient-containment theorem.

public_sources.title: Improved Online Conformal Prediction via Strongly Adaptive Online Learning
public_sources.authors: Aadyot Bhatnagar, Huan Wang, Caiming Xiong, Yu Bai
public_sources.result: Strongly adaptive regret/coverage over many subintervals is a plausible way to make calibration react to local drift, but its guarantee remains approximate interval-level conformal coverage, not a theorem for dependent stratified-SMC influence coefficients.

public_sources.title: Variance estimation in the particle filter
public_sources.result: Single-run genealogy variance decomposition and variable-particle allocation remain the theorem benchmark for the resampling regime covered by that work; no new theorem-clean transfer to the independent-stratified multi-generation implementation was established here.

public_sources.title: Adaptive online variance estimation in particle filters: the ALVar estimator
public_sources.result: Supports genealogy as an online variance/drift diagnostic under its assumptions, but does not make the r125 lag-4 coalescence increment a calibrated per-generation coefficient estimator for the independent-stratified stress.

synthetic_validation.model: Exact same 12-generation two-state Feynman-Kac model, independent stratified resampling, 768 total particles/run, continuation CV^2 coefficient proxy and lag-4 genealogy coalescence increment as r125.

scenarios.abrupt: 20 runs shock generation 2 then 40 runs generation 9
scenarios.gradual: 60 runs fractional shock position linearly 1 to 9
scenarios.recurring: two cycles of generations 1,4,7,10 held 10 runs each

synthetic_validation.discovery: A small disjoint discovery grid varied genealogy-dominance thresholds, disagreement distance, cooldown length, beta cap and uncertainty inflation. It confirmed a tradeoff: hard genealogy alarms can improve uncertainty-box coverage and sometimes reduce transients, but noisy dominant-generation changes cause frequent clamping.

frozen_alarm_controller.trigger: After a completed run, fire if lag-4 genealogy dominant generation changes by at least 2 from the previous run OR differs by at least 1 from the pre-run continuation-center dominant generation, provided top genealogy share / second share >=1.25.
frozen_alarm_controller.normal_mode: r125 uncertainty-aware beta selection with conditional 1.30 box cap

synthetic_validation.validation: 12 disjoint streams per controller per scenario; the frozen alarm controller was not retuned on these streams. Exact schedule ratios use true A only post hoc; particle schedules use only completed-run diagnostics.

derived_results.claim: The frozen genealogy-triggered hard cooldown did not robustly solve the stale-coefficient transient problem. Versus r125 uncertainty control, it improved gradual box coverage from 0.675 to 0.8375 and slightly reduced the recurring worst exact ratio from 1.3211 to 1.3091, but worsened mean exact ratios in all three scenarios and was active roughly 63-68% of runs. This makes the chosen hard OR alarm too noisy/costly for adoption.

The fixed beta=0.5 controller remained much stronger on tested worst transients: recurring worst 1.0776 versus 1.3091 for the hard alarm and 1.3211 for uncertainty control. Its average allocation efficiency is lower, so the problem is to interpolate defensively rather than switch on a noisy genealogy event.

Given r125 magnitude miscalibration and r126 frequent alarms, genealogy is better treated as a risk/localization covariate that changes the allowed concentration continuously or raises a calibration budget, rather than as a binary command that overwrites beta for a fixed cooldown.

Adaptive/strongly-adaptive online conformal methods can provide distribution-free long-run or interval-level coverage-frequency control under shift and are plausible wrappers for a moving residual scale. They do not by themselves supply per-run containment of the true normalized influence vector, so they cannot justify an unconditional per-run variance-inflation cap without an additional one-step or model-specific layer.

The targeted source search again did not identify a theorem-clean single-run generation-wise variance estimator specifically established for the independent-stratified multi-generation particle filter used here. This remains a search result, not a nonexistence claim.

negative_or_scope_evidence: The alarm validation is a synthetic two-state particle model; it is not a real-agent or AGI performance result.
The frozen hard alarm was selected from a small discovery grid; validation was disjoint, but this does not establish broad optimality of the trigger family.
Normalized Z MSE is noisy and did not consistently improve with the hard alarm; exact separable schedule ratio remains the primary metric.
Online conformal coverage frequency is not equivalent to one-step coefficient containment or a pathwise variance cap.
No genealogy theorem was silently transferred from multinomial/adaptive-resampling settings to the independent-stratified implementation.
frontier: Replace binary genealogy cooldown with a continuous defensive concentration controller: use continuation for coefficient magnitude, and map genealogy disagreement/localized drift to a predictable maximum beta or uniform reserve fraction. Target graceful interpolation between r125 uncertainty control and fixed beta=0.5.

Calibrate the continuation residual scale with an online method that has an explicit guarantee matching the desired object. Explore strongly-adaptive/online conformal residual calibration for frequency guarantees, while keeping the per-run 1.30 cap labeled conditional until a one-step or model-specific certificate exists.

Build a two-timescale controller: fast genealogy disagreement changes reserve immediately; slower continuation residual calibration determines how quickly concentration is restored. Tune on discovery streams and validate once on disjoint abrupt/gradual/recurring streams.
Continue targeted theorem search for independent-stratified single-run generation-wise variance estimation; keep genealogy as localizer if the theorem gap remains.
Extend to 20 generations and terminal boundary diagnostics after the risk-controller semantics are stable.
exact_next_action: Keep the r125 continuation estimator and abandon the r126 frozen hard-OR cooldown as an adoption candidate. Define a continuous risk score from genealogy localization confidence and disagreement with the continuation center, and set beta_max_t = 0.5 + 0.4*exp(-k*risk_t) or an equivalent monotone reserve rule, with no genealogy magnitude used as A. Tune k and a short risk-memory decay on one discovery seed family, freeze them, then validate once on disjoint abrupt/gradual/recurring streams against uncertainty and fixed-beta=0.5 using mean/worst/p95 exact ratio, box coverage, alarm/risk duty cycle and normalized Z MSE. In parallel, test online/strongly-adaptive conformal calibration only as a coverage-frequency layer and state explicitly why it does not create a per-run variance certificate.
